description: Direct check of C-bootstrap-partial-state: call BootstrapCluster against a store whose StoreLog fails once, then observe whether the same store remains bootstrappable. The oracle is that a second BootstrapCluster on the now-healthy store seeds the configuration entry (retry_allowed == true); identity is the storage instance labelled on every event. Because the term write precedes the log write and the existing-state guard reads the term, observing retry_allowed false is the violating observation for the bounded recovery responsibility.

harness.description: In-package Go test that runs BootstrapCluster on a fresh in-memory store with a single simulated StoreLog failure, checks HasExistingState afterwards, then retries BootstrapCluster on the now-healthy store and reports both outcomes.
semantic_changes: The LogStore wrapper fails exactly one StoreLog call to expose the ordering between the term write and the configuration-entry write; all other store behaviour is the in-repository InmemStore.
Protocol version 3 is used so the seeded entry is a LogConfiguration entry; no protocol logic is altered.

legality.derivation: BootstrapCluster is a public function that accepts caller-supplied LogStore and StableStore implementations, and the LogStore interface permits StoreLog to return an error, so a store that fails that call after the stable write is a legal object. The retry uses the same function and a healthy store, which is exactly the sequence an operator would attempt.
legality.applicability: The store starts clean (HasExistingState false), the configuration lists the local server as a single voter, and only one StoreLog call is simulated to fail; the proposition is local to this store instance.
unresolved: Whether a production store fails StoreLog in this position.
alternatives: RecoverCluster is an operator path that can force a configuration onto such a store, which bounds but does not remove the blocked retry.

grounding.derivation: The guard is what decides whether the seed may run again, and the observed log index shows whether the seed actually completed; reporting both lets the comparison distinguish a genuine already-bootstrapped store from one whose term exists without its configuration entry.
grounding.applicability: Admitted only for the store instance that experienced the simulated failure, correlated by the storage label shared between the prerequisite and the result event.
alternatives: A retry failure on an already-bootstrapped store would be correct behaviour; the harness reports the log index so that case is distinguishable.

observable_properties.description: After a bootstrap attempt fails at the log store, a subsequent attempt on the healthy store must still be able to seed the configuration entry; the compared field combines the retry error with the observed log index.

uncertainties: The check uses an in-memory store with a single simulated failure; it establishes the local bootstrap responsibility, not a cluster-wide consequence, and does not exercise RecoverCluster.
Only the single-StoreLog failure point is instantiated.
